title: Getting dressed for the weather
paragraphs: My name is Timur Bekzhanov. I am twenty years old and I come from Kostanay — a city in northern Kazakhstan, famous for its cold winters and wide, flat landscapes. I study Architecture at WKU in Uralsk. I am in my second year now. I love architecture partly because it connects buildings with the environment — and that means thinking about weather all the time. How a building protects you from wind, cold, or heat is one of the most important questions in design. So naturally, I think about weather a lot. And that means I also think a lot about clothes.

In summer, getting dressed is easy. The weather in Uralsk in July is hot — sometimes thirty-two or thirty-three degrees. On those days, I wear a plain white t-shirt, light cotton trousers, and canvas shoes. Everything is loose, light, and breathable. I almost never wear a jacket in July — it would be too warm and uncomfortable. My summer look is simple, but I prefer simple. Good design, I always say, does not need unnecessary decoration.

Autumn is my favourite season for fashion. The weather is cool and crisp — usually between five and fifteen degrees. On a typical October morning, I wear a dark green woollen jumper over a white shirt, dark jeans, and brown leather boots. If it is rainy, I add a long waterproof jacket — dark navy blue, with a hood. I sometimes carry a compact folding umbrella in my bag as well, just in case. The combination of warm, layered clothes and cool, fresh air makes me feel alert and ready for anything.

Winter requires a completely different approach. When the temperature falls below minus ten, I dress in layers. First, a thin thermal base layer. Then a thick dark blue sweater. On top, my warmest coat — a long, charcoal-grey wool coat that falls to the knee. Around my neck, a warm cream-coloured scarf. On my hands, black leather gloves. On my feet, waterproof boots with a thick rubber sole. My hat is a dark grey knitted one that covers my ears completely. When I am dressed like this, even minus fifteen degrees is bearable. The key is covering every part of the body.

Spring is the most unpredictable season. One day can be ten degrees and sunny; the next can be minus five with snowfall. On those uncertain spring days, I use what fashion people call "the layering method." I leave the dormitory wearing a medium-weight jacket over a light hoodie. I carry gloves in my pocket, just in case. I wear waterproof ankle boots — not too warm, not too light. If the sun comes out, I can remove the jacket and tie it around my waist. If it gets cold again, I put it back on. Flexibility is the key.

People sometimes ask me: "Timur, you always look well dressed — how do you do it?" My answer is always the same. I do not buy expensive clothes. I buy practical, well-made clothes in neutral colours — dark blue, grey, white, brown, black — that work in all weather. A good coat, a warm scarf, and a pair of good boots are more important than ten fashionable items. Dress for the weather first. Style comes naturally after that.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: Timur! You always look so well dressed. What are you wearing today?

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: Just layers — a white shirt, dark green jumper, and my navy waterproof jacket.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: Is that jacket warm enough? It's only five degrees outside!

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: With two layers underneath, yes — completely warm. Layering is the secret.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: What do you wear when it's really cold — like minus fifteen?

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: My long wool coat, a thick sweater, leather gloves, and my warmest boots.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: And the scarf — I always see you with that cream-coloured one.

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: It's woollen and very warm. My grandmother knitted it for me in Kostanay.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: What do you do in spring when the weather changes every day?

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: I layer. A medium jacket plus a light hoodie underneath — I can adjust as needed.

dialogue.speaker: Aizat
dialogue.text: What's your advice for dressing well as a student on a budget?

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: Buy neutral colours and practical items. A good coat and good boots — that's it.
